scene.label: Act 5, Scene 10
scene.title: SCENE X. Another part of the plain.

content.text: Enter Aeneas, Paris, Antenor and Deiphobus.

lines.text: Stand, ho! yet are we masters of the field.
lines.plainText: Stand ho yet are we masters of the field

lines.text: Never go home; here starve we out the night.
lines.plainText: Never go home here starve we out the night

lines.text: Hector is slain.
lines.plainText: Hector is slain

lines.text: Hector! The gods forbid!
lines.plainText: Hector The gods forbid

lines.text: He's dead, and at the murderer's horse's tail,
lines.plainText: He's dead and at the murderer's horse's tail

lines.text: In beastly sort, dragg'd through the shameful field.
lines.plainText: In beastly sort dragg'd through the shameful field

lines.text: Frown on, you heavens, effect your rage with speed.
lines.plainText: Frown on you heavens effect your rage with speed

lines.text: Sit, gods, upon your thrones, and smile at Troy.
lines.plainText: Sit gods upon your thrones and smile at Troy

lines.text: I say at once let your brief plagues be mercy,
lines.plainText: I say at once let your brief plagues be mercy

lines.text: And linger not our sure destructions on.
lines.plainText: And linger not our sure destructions on

lines.text: My lord, you do discomfort all the host.
lines.plainText: My lord you do discomfort all the host

lines.text: You understand me not that tell me so.
lines.plainText: You understand me not that tell me so

lines.text: I do not speak of flight, of fear of death,
lines.plainText: I do not speak of flight of fear of death

lines.text: But dare all imminence that gods and men
lines.plainText: But dare all imminence that gods and men

lines.text: Address their dangers in. Hector is gone.
lines.plainText: Address their dangers in Hector is gone

lines.text: Who shall tell Priam so, or Hecuba?
lines.plainText: Who shall tell Priam so or Hecuba

lines.text: Let him that will a screech-owl aye be call'd
lines.plainText: Let him that will a screechowl aye be call'd

lines.text: Go in to Troy, and say there 'Hector's dead.'
lines.plainText: Go in to Troy and say there 'Hector's dead'

lines.text: There is a word will Priam turn to stone;
lines.plainText: There is a word will Priam turn to stone

lines.text: Make wells and Niobes of the maids and wives,
lines.plainText: Make wells and Niobes of the maids and wives

lines.text: Cold statues of the youth; and, in a word,
lines.plainText: Cold statues of the youth and in a word

lines.text: Scare Troy out of itself. But, march away;
lines.plainText: Scare Troy out of itself But march away

lines.text: Hector is dead; there is no more to say.
lines.plainText: Hector is dead there is no more to say

lines.text: Stay yet. You vile abominable tents,
lines.plainText: Stay yet You vile abominable tents

lines.text: Thus proudly pight upon our Phrygian plains,
lines.plainText: Thus proudly pight upon our Phrygian plains

lines.text: Let Titan rise as early as he dare,
lines.plainText: Let Titan rise as early as he dare

lines.text: I'll through and through you. And, thou great-siz'd coward,
lines.plainText: I'll through and through you And thou greatsiz'd coward

lines.text: No space of earth shall sunder our two hates;
lines.plainText: No space of earth shall sunder our two hates

lines.text: I'll haunt thee like a wicked conscience still,
lines.plainText: I'll haunt thee like a wicked conscience still

lines.text: That mouldeth goblins swift as frenzy's thoughts.
lines.plainText: That mouldeth goblins swift as frenzy's thoughts

lines.text: Strike a free march to Troy. With comfort go;
lines.plainText: Strike a free march to Troy With comfort go

lines.text: Hope of revenge shall hide our inward woe.
lines.plainText: Hope of revenge shall hide our inward woe

lines.text: But hear you, hear you!
lines.plainText: But hear you hear you

lines.text: Hence, broker-lackey. Ignominy and shame
lines.plainText: Hence brokerlackey Ignominy and shame

lines.text: Pursue thy life, and live aye with thy name!
lines.plainText: Pursue thy life and live aye with thy name

lines.text: A goodly medicine for my aching bones! O world! world! Thus is the poor agent despis'd! O traitors and bawds, how earnestly are you set a-work, and how ill requited! Why should our endeavour be so lov'd, and the performance so loathed? What verse for it? What instance for it? Let me see—
